```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(agecraft)
```

All bounds are nonnegative whole numbers. An interval `[1,5)` includes 1 and
excludes 5, and prints `1-4`. Units describe the age coordinates. Missing ranges
have both bounds missing. Fractional bounds are rejected without rounding.

## Genealogy: reconcile records at the same reference date

Suppose two records imply that a person was aged `[20,25)` and `[23,28)` years
on January 1, 1900. These bounds must already refer to that shared date. The
package does not infer a birth-date range or advance a record's age to another
date automatically.

```{r genealogy}
record_a <- age_group(20, 25, unit = "year")
record_b <- age_group(23, 28, unit = "year")
compare_age_groups(record_a, record_b) # [23,25), printed 23-24
contradiction <- compare_age_groups(record_a, age_group(30, 35, unit = "year"),
                                    keep_empty = TRUE)
contradiction # status empty, missing intersection bounds
```

An empty intersection indicates contradictory ranges under these assumptions.
A `missing` status instead indicates unavailable evidence. The default crosswalk
omits both empty and missing pairs; `keep_empty = TRUE` distinguishes them.

For relatives whose possible ages are `[20,25)` and `[40,45)` at the same date,
the second person's age minus the first's is strictly between 15 and 25 years.
Those are exclusive bounds on real-valued ages, not completed-age differences.

```{r genealogy-gap}
compare_age_groups(record_a, age_group(40, 45, unit = "year"), "age_gap")
```

## Sociology: compare survey definitions and uncertain assignment

Survey A uses `[0,18)` and `[18,65)` years; survey B uses `[0,5)`, `[5,25)`,
and `[25,65)`. The expected nonempty crosswalk contains `[0,5)`, `[5,18)`,
`[18,25)`, and `[25,65)`, retaining the source row identifiers and labels.

```{r surveys}
a <- age_group(c(0, 18), c(18, 65), unit = "year")
b <- age_group(c(0, 5, 25), c(5, 25, 65), unit = "year")
compare_age_groups(a, b)
```

A reported age range `[17,19)` crosses A's boundary at 18: neither assignment
is definite, while both are possible. Definite membership means containment;
possible membership means nonempty overlap. Touching endpoints do not overlap.

```{r uncertain-membership}
reported <- age_group(17, 19, unit = "year")
compare_age_groups(reported, a, "membership")
compare_age_groups(reported, a, "membership", membership = "possible")
# Request ambiguous = "warn" or "error" to flag multiple possible matches.
categorize_age(reported, by = a, output = "interval") # Missing assignment
```

Age bands are not birth cohorts. A birth cohort requires a reference date and
calendar assumptions; labelling a band alone does not establish cohort membership.

## Economics: study coverage and household age gaps

A study defines working age as `[18,65)` years. Published data use `[15,25)`,
`[25,55)`, and `[55,75)`. Intersections are `[18,25)`, `[25,55)`, and `[55,65)`.
The crosswalk does not determine what share of a published band's count belongs
to the study: that requires finer observations or explicit allocation assumptions.

```{r economics}
study <- age_group(18, 65, unit = "year")
published <- age_group(c(15, 25, 55), c(25, 55, 75), unit = "year")
compare_age_groups(study, published)
# Excluding [25,55) leaves disjoint [18,25) and [55,65) coverage:
compare_age_groups(study, published[2], "difference")
compare_age_groups(study, operation = "width") # 47 years of age coordinates
```

Household ages `[30,35)` and `[32,37)` measured at a common survey date permit
a second-minus-first age gap strictly between -3 and 7 years. The order is
unresolved because the ranges overlap. Missing evidence yields missing bounds.

```{r household}
person_a <- age_group(c(30, NA), c(35, NA), unit = "year")
person_b <- age_group(32, 37, unit = "year")
compare_age_groups(person_a, person_b, "age_gap")
compare_age_groups(person_a, person_b, "ordering")
```

## Set coverage versus crosswalks

`operation = "intersection"`, `"union"`, and `"difference"` operate on overall
coverage using ivs set semantics; they can merge adjacent source groups and
preserve gaps. Use `"crosswalk"` when the source-group identities matter.
Comparisons require matching units, including on empty vectors. Convert inputs
explicitly before comparison. Calendar shifting and automatic conversion of
record ages to a shared date are intentionally deferred until their reference-date
semantics are specified.
